expected.sentence: Six years, commuted to four years on July 17; paroled from Leavenworth on September 16, 1920.

operations.source: Primary appellate opinion Isenhouer v United States,256F842: https://openjurist.org/256/f1d/842/isenhouer-v-united-states . Identifies originating trial judge, distinguished from appellate author Hook. No initial arrest from sentence date.

operations.name: Clure Isenhouer

expected.name: Clure Isenhouer
expected.description: Clure Isenhouer was prosecuted under United States wartime statutes of the World War I era (chiefly the Espionage Act, the Sedition Act, or the Selective Service Act). Recorded offense: Conspiracy. Sentence: Commuted from 6 to 4 years July 17. Sentenced October 6, 1917. Held at the Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary. Later disposition: Paroled from Leavenworth. This case is documented in the 1921 U.S. Senate hearing "Amnesty and Pardon for Political Prisoners" (digitized by the Internet Archive).

operations.source: Primary National Archives Leavenworth inmate case-file index https://www.archives.gov/kansas-city/finding-aids/leavenworth-penitentiary/inmates-i-j-k.html identifies Isenhouer,Clure12002. Historical Leavenworth number, not a modern BOP register number.

operations.name: Ben Legg

expected.name: Ben Legg
expected.description: Ben Legg was one of the 74 Industrial Workers of the World members held in the Snohomish County jail and charged with murder after the Everett Massacre. On November 5, 1916, some 300 Industrial Workers of the World members sailed from Seattle to Everett, Washington aboard the steamers Verona and Calista to support a shingle-weavers' strike and the IWW's free-speech fight. At the Everett dock, Snohomish County sheriff Donald McRae and a posse of armed vigilantes opened fire on the Verona, killing at least five Wobblies and wounding dozens. The returning IWW members were arrested, and 74 were charged with the murder of two deputies (Jefferson Beard and Charles Curtis) killed in the gunfire. Only Thomas H. Tracy was brought to trial; after his acquittal on May 5, 1917, the charges against the others were dropped.

operations.source: Everett Public Library booking photograph roster reproduced by University of Washington IWW History Project: https://depts.washington.edu/iww/faces_of_iww.shtml . Individually identifies Ben Legg, IWW prisoner4880, matching existing case. Historical1916booking number, not BOP.

expected.description: Louis Morgan was one of the 74 Industrial Workers of the World members held in the Snohomish County jail and charged with murder after the Everett Massacre. On November 5, 1916, some 300 Industrial Workers of the World members sailed from Seattle to Everett, Washington aboard the steamers Verona and Calista to support a shingle-weavers' strike and the IWW's free-speech fight. At the Everett dock, Snohomish County sheriff Donald McRae and a posse of armed vigilantes opened fire on the Verona, killing at least five Wobblies and wounding dozens. The returning IWW members were arrested, and 74 were charged with the murder of two deputies (Jefferson Beard and Charles Curtis) killed in the gunfire. Only Thomas H. Tracy was brought to trial; after his acquittal on May 5, 1917, the charges against the others were dropped. At the time of the massacre he was 24, a laborer, born in Texas.
